nodes.label: Local Windows PC Guide
nodes.rationale: A ten-step guide written against one specific install (this Windows 11 machine, Python 3.13.2, existing .venv) rather than generically, so every path and command can be pasted verbatim. The PC has to be awake - nothing publishes while it is asleep or shut down, and uploads resume within about five minutes of waking.

nodes.label: Single-Process Local Deployment
nodes.rationale: On a server the web tier and the scheduler are split so that several web workers cannot each run the schedule; on one PC a single waitress process with SCHEDULER_ENABLED=1 does both, which is simpler and means one background task is enough. The 'Scheduler started' line on startup is the confirmation that the automation is running inside the web process.

nodes.label: Data Folder Outside OneDrive
nodes.rationale: The project lives inside a synced OneDrive folder. If the bot stored videos there, OneDrive would try to upload every clip to the cloud and could lock the database file mid-write. DATA_ROOT, MEDIA_ROOT and LOG_ROOT therefore point at C:\Users\tolia\SocialBotData, inside the user profile but outside the synced tree.

nodes.label: .env Byte-Order-Mark Hazard
nodes.rationale: The .env file is generated with [System.IO.File]::WriteAllLines rather than Set-Content -Encoding utf8, because the latter prepends a byte-order mark that makes the first key parse as \ufeffAPP_ENV and be silently ignored. Bytes 239 187 191 at the head of the file are the tell; Notepad's plain 'UTF-8' save option adds one too. SQLAlchemy database URLs use forward slashes even on Windows.

nodes.label: Windows Task Scheduler Background Task
nodes.rationale: A 'SocialMediaBot' scheduled task runs waitress-serve at logon and restarts it on crash. -LogonType S4U is what suppresses the console window (and is why the registration block needs an Administrator prompt), -ExecutionTimeLimit 0 stops Windows killing a task meant to run forever, -RestartCount 3 recovers from crashes, -AllowStartIfOnBatteries keeps it alive unplugged, and -MultipleInstances IgnoreNew prevents a second copy. LastTaskResult 267009 means running; 0 means it exited. Without -Principal it still works but leaves a console window that must not be closed.

nodes.label: Loopback-Only Binding (HOST=127.0.0.1)
nodes.rationale: Binding to the loopback address means the site is reachable from this PC and nowhere else, so no firewall rule is needed and nobody on the network or the internet can reach it. Changing HOST to 0.0.0.0 to reach it from a phone is explicitly refused as advice because it would expose a login page over unencrypted HTTP to the whole network - real remote access means deploying properly with HTTPS. APP_ENV stays production locally because development mode would expose an interactive Python console to anything that reaches the port; FORCE_HTTPS=0 because there is no certificate on localhost.

nodes.label: Broken python on PATH (Microsoft Store Stub)
nodes.rationale: Typing bare python reaches the Microsoft Store stub, which prints 'Python was not found' instead of running Python. The real interpreter is fine, just not first on PATH, so every command in the guide uses .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe and .\.venv\Scripts\flask.exe explicitly.

nodes.label: PowerShell 5.1 Syntax Constraints
nodes.rationale: The shell here is Windows PowerShell 5.1, where &&, || and ?: do not exist. Commands chain with ; and conditional execution uses if ($?) { }.

nodes.label: UTC Publishing Times and Timezone Conversion
nodes.rationale: Publishing slots are stored and entered in UTC, never local time. On a Pacific-time PC the 09:00/15:00/20:00 defaults land at 02:00/08:00/13:00 local, so the first slot would fire at 2 a.m. when the machine is probably asleep and nothing would publish. Convert with UTC = local + 7 hours in PDT or + 8 in PST, and re-check after the clocks change in March and November.

nodes.label: localhost OAuth Redirect URI
nodes.rationale: Google allows plain http for localhost, so http://localhost:8000/accounts/oauth/callback/youtube works without a certificate. It must say localhost and not 127.0.0.1, because that is what PUBLIC_BASE_URL says. Changing the port means updating four things: PORT and PUBLIC_BASE_URL in .env, the --listen argument in the scheduled task, and the redirect URI in Google Cloud.

nodes.label: ffmpeg Install on Windows
nodes.rationale: winget install Gyan.FFmpeg, then a NEW PowerShell window - the installer changes PATH and an already-open window will not see it, which is almost always the cause of 'ffmpeg still not found'. If it is genuinely off PATH, set FFMPEG_BINARY and FFPROBE_BINARY to full paths. Excluding the media folder from Windows Defender real-time scanning noticeably speeds up conversion, since ffmpeg is CPU-bound.

nodes.label: Local Backup Procedure
nodes.rationale: Two things cannot be recreated: .env (because of ENCRYPTION_KEY) and the database. A date-stamped copy of both into C:\Users\tolia\SocialBotBackup is the whole backup.
